output.subject: We have received your message about your husband's mortgage payment
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us, and we are so sorry to hear about your husband's stroke. We hope he is getting the care he needs, and we know it is a lot to manage the household bills on top of everything else right now.

We have received your complaint. Here is what you told us:

- Your husband set up automatic payments on the mortgage years ago, but you mentioned that this month's payment was never drafted.
- A late fee of $87.40 now appears on the loan, even though you have his checking statement showing the money was there the whole time.
- The mortgage is in your husband's name only, and he cannot speak on the phone with us at the moment.

You asked us to reverse the late fee and to take the payment.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days. We are sorry for the stress this has added during an already difficult time.

With best wishes to you and your husband,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The loan is in the husband's name only; confirm what the customer is authorized to discuss or do on this loan before sharing any loan details or taking instructions from her.
Customer asks for the $87.40 late fee to be reversed; the draft only acknowledges this, so the decision is yours.
Customer asks for the missed payment to be taken; decide how the payment can be made and by whom, given the authorization question.
Check why the autopay did not draft this month and whether the enrollment was still active.
Customer says she has a checking statement showing sufficient funds; decide whether to request it.
Borrower is hospitalized after a stroke on 9/14 and cannot communicate; consider whether hardship or vulnerable-customer support applies and add specifics if so.
Consider whether the missed payment risks further fees or credit reporting while this is under review, as she may need to know urgently.
The complaint uses two different name tokens for the husband (⟦NAME_1⟧ and ⟦NAME_2⟧); the draft avoids both, so confirm this before sending.
